q: A segment tree answers a range-sum query in…
why: It combines O(log n) stored ranges.

q: Range sums on an array that never changes. Best tool?
why: O(1) per query after O(n) setup; a segment tree only pays off when there are updates.

q: A Bloom filter says an item is NOT present. Can it be wrong?
options: No: a zero bit means it was never added
why: False negatives are impossible; only false positives happen.

q: Why can a Bloom filter give a false positive?
options: Other items may have set every bit this item hashes to
It stores items in a list
why: All k bits can be 1 because of different items.

q: Why do databases use B+ trees for indexes?
options: Wide nodes make the tree very shallow, so a lookup needs few disk reads
why: Disk reads dominate the cost; a height of 3–4 covers billions of rows.

q: In a Fenwick tree, what is i & −i for i = 12 (1100)?
why: It isolates the lowest set bit: 0100 = 4.
